message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have the ability to hit the VirusTotal servers myself – there’s no “VirusTotal” helper function exposed in this sandbox.  
What I *can* give you is a quick recipe so you can pull those records yourself from your own machine (or CI job) without exposing your key in public chat.

---

### Quick‑start: Pull up to 10 files that communicated with `12.234.56.126`

#### 1️⃣ Pick the right API version  

| Version | Endpoint pattern |
|---------|------------------|
| **v5**  | `/ip_addresses/{ipv4_address}/communicating_files` |
| **v2**  | `/ip_addresses/{ipv4_address}` → then look at `"communicating_files"` field |

> If you’re still on the legacy v2 API, upgrade ASAP—V5 has better rate limits & richer payloads.

Below I’ll show both variants just in case.

---

#### 2️⃣ Build the URL

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v{VERSION}/{resource}
```

For V5:

```text
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v5/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/communicating_files
```

For V2:

```text
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126
```

(then parse the JSON response.)

---

#### 3️⃣ Add parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| `limit`   | Max items per page (`max_number_to_retrieve`) | `limit=10` |
| `cursor`  | Pagination token (`continuation_cursor`) | `cursor:pointer` |

So the full query string becomes:

```
?limit=10&cursor=pointer
```

Putting it together (V5):

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v5/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/communicating_files?limit=10&cursor=pointer
```

---

#### 4️⃣ Authentication header

Use your API key in the `x-apikey` header (recommended over query params).

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: my_api" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v5/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/communicating_files?limit=10&cursor=pointer"
```

If you prefer the older style:

```bash
curl -G --data-urlencode "apikey=my_api" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126"
```

---

#### 5️⃣ Inspect the response

A typical V5 reply looks like:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "file_id_123",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
    "next": "...?cursor=new_pointer..."
  }
}
```

Take the first ten entries under `"data"`.  
If you want more than one page, follow the `"next"` link until you’ve collected all desired results.

---

### A few extra tips

| Tip | Why |
|-----|-----|
| Store `my_api` in a `.env` file or secret manager instead of hard‑coding it into scripts | Keeps credentials out of source control |
| Respect the rate limits (default ~4 requests/sec for free tier) | Avoid getting throttled |
| Cache responses locally when re-running analyses | Saves bandwidth & time |

---

That’s basically everything you need! Run the above `curl` (or translate it into Python/PowerShell/etc.) and you’ll see the list of files that touched that IP. Let me know if you run into any hiccups while wiring it up.
